links.outcome: Ability of uncertainty measures to detect artificially degraded images at low, medium, high magnitudes
links.effect: Test time augmentation vs probability entropy AUC: low 0.54 vs 0.68 (as reported), medium 0.70 vs 0.82, high 0.83 vs 0.90; detection weak at low degradation for some methods.
links.quote: Test time augmentation and probability entropy respectively achieved the highest and lowest degraded image detection at low (AUC = 0.54 vs. 0.68), medium (AUC = 0.70 vs. 0.82), and high (AUC = 0.83 vs. 0.90) degradation magnitudes.

unlisted_practices: Comparing uncertainty quantification methods (test time augmentation, MC dropout, deep ensembles, entropy) for detecting false positives and recovering false negatives in imaging segmentation

links.effect: TTA was superior overall; FP detection AUCs ranged 0.77-0.81; correlations were mixed, with best ρ values 0.57, 0.72, 0.35, and 0.96.
links.quote: Performance for the correlation analysis was mixed, where the strongest performance was achieved by test time augmentation for SUV<sub>total</sub>capture (ρ= 0.57) and segmentation Dice coefficient (ρ= 0.72), by Monte Carlo dropout for SUV<sub>mean</sub>capture (ρ= 0.35), and by probability entropy for segmentation cross entropy (ρ= 0.96).

links.effect: Degraded image detection varied by method and magnitude: low AUC = 0.54 vs. 0.68, medium AUC = 0.70 vs. 0.82, high AUC = 0.83 vs. 0.90.
links.quote: Test time augmentation and probability entropy respectively achieved the highest and lowest degraded image detection at low (AUC = 0.54 vs. 0.68), medium (AUC = 0.70 vs. 0.82), and high (AUC = 0.83 vs. 0.90) degradation magnitudes.

links.outcome: uncertainty quantification performance in detecting false positives and degraded images
links.effect: All UQ methods achieved strong FP detection (AUC 0.77-0.81); test time augmentation achieved superior performance, while probability entropy performed worst
links.quote: For detecting FPs, all UQ methods achieve strong performance, with AUC values ranging narrowly between 0.77 and 0.81.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates multiple post-hoc and intrinsic uncertainty quantification (UQ) methods as safeguards/reliability checks to detect degraded images and model errors (false positives/false negatives) in lesion segmentation.
